rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The intermediate temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.
Raise temperature while holding the gradient fixed to test selectivity around the sole unresolved pair. The current time margin allows this targeted change without needing to steepen the gradient.

The central cluster suggests an elution-order crossover between 40 and 50 C; a further 5 C increase may separate that pair beyond the crossover. This smaller temperature step also limits compression of the neighboring pair whose resolution decreased at 50 C.
The maximum CRF is already achieved; shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Retain injection 3 as the benchmark if either marginal pair falls below R = 1.5.

The faster gradient loses resolution at 55 C, so test a substantially cooler selectivity regime rather than further compressing that marginal cluster. Injection 3 remains the maximum-score fallback while we search for a faster fully resolved method.

Test an intermediate temperature on the shorter gradient to seek a selectivity window between the crowded 25 C pattern and the central-pair crossover near 45 C. Keep the fully resolved 12-minute, 55 C method as the fallback.

Return to the fully resolved temperature and gradient duration, but raise the starting organic fraction one step to advance elution. The slightly shallower gradient may help preserve resolution of the two marginal pairs while shortening the observed elution window.

Test a faster, hotter regime that may move the current limiting pair through its selectivity crossover and separate it in reversed order. This exploratory run retains the broad solvent range, with injection 3 already securing the maximum CRF.

Slightly reduce the slope relative to injection 7 to recover its sole deficient pair while retaining the higher starting organic fraction. This tests whether full resolution can be restored with an elution time close to, or slightly shorter than, injection 3.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction changes selectivity enough to resolve the two deficient pairs in the fast 60 C regime. This explores a substantially shorter alternative while preserving injection 3 as the maximum-score fallback.

Test a shallower gradient at 35 C to expand the crowded central cluster seen in injection 6 and potentially establish a second fully resolved selectivity window. The last peak is expected to remain near, but below, the 10-minute scoring threshold.

Slightly flatten the successful gradient to improve the narrow resolution margin of the earlier critical pair while checking that the later pair remains fully resolved. The modest increase in retention should still leave the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

Explore a steeper gradient at a moderately high temperature to test a different elution-order regime for the central cluster. This may offer a much faster fully resolved alternative; injections 3 and 12 already secure the maximum score.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient at 40 C to change selectivity and expand the central cluster. This may resolve the deficient pair from injection 1 while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes; injection 3 remains the best confirmed method.

Flatten the gradient from injection 7 to restore its deficient pair while retaining the improved separation of the later critical pair. This targets a fully resolved method with more resolution margin than injection 3 and a last peak still below 10 minutes.

Raise the starting organic fraction from injection 14 to advance the late peak and further flatten the gradient, potentially lifting its sole deficient pair above R = 1.5. Check the early peaks for compression while retaining injection 3 as the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Refine the fully resolved 55 C regime by combining a shallower gradient with a modestly higher starting organic fraction. This targets greater resolution margin while keeping the final peak below 10 minutes; injection 3 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Shorten the programmed gradient while preserving injection 3’s successful slope and temperature. Because all peaks previously eluted before this new gradient ends, this should retain full resolution and maximum CRF with a lower final organic fraction.

Shorten the programmed gradient another step while preserving the fully resolved slope of injections 3 and 18. The gradient reaches its final composition at the outlet at 8.65 minutes, after the observed last peak at 7.60 minutes, so the separation should remain unchanged.

Raise temperature one grid step from injection 19 to test whether the shortened program can deliver full resolution with earlier elution. If selectivity deteriorates, retain the confirmed 55 C method rather than trading resolution for speed.

Slightly flatten injection 17’s gradient to lift its sole deficient pair from R = 1.41 toward full resolution, while preserving the later pair’s margin. This targets another maximum-score method with improved minimum resolution and an expected last peak below 10 minutes.

Test a modest slope increase between the fully resolved benchmark and injection 4’s overly steep gradient. This seeks earlier final elution while checking whether the limiting pair can retain R ≥ 1.5; injection 19 remains the confirmed fallback.

Use a slightly shallower slope than injection 9 to lift its R = 1.47 pair above full resolution while retaining the higher starting organic fraction. This targets maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient and earlier final elution than injection 15.

Shorten the programmed gradient while preserving the successful slope through the critical cluster and the first nine peaks. The final peak will encounter the hold and may elute later, so this tests whether the narrower solvent window retains maximum CRF without pushing it beyond 10 minutes.

Refine injection 23 with a slightly shallower slope to improve its limiting pair while shortening the programmed gradient to eight minutes. This should preserve maximum CRF with both critical pairs above 1.5; injection 19 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method with the shortest gradient program.
